question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}23 & -19 & 13 \\ 50 & -43 & 32 \\ 30 & -27 & 22\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & a & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & b & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $a+b.$
question.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$ 

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Computing $A-(-2)I,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}23 & -19 & 13 \\ 50 & -43 & 32 \\ 30 & -27 & 22\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}25 & -19 & 13 \\ 50 & -41 & 32 \\ 30 & -27 & 24\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ that we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}25 & -19 & 13 & 0 \\ 50 & -41 & 32 & 0 \\ 30 & -27 & 24 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{6}{5}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}25 & -19 & 13 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{21}{5} & \frac{42}{5} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{7}{5}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}25 & -19 & 13 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$  Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$ 
Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 2 \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+b=1+1=2.$
